length.text: Usually 3 to 4 ft; up to about 6.8 ft

diet.text: Rodents, lizards, eggs and snakes, even rattlesnakes

overview.text: The Desert Kingsnake is a yellow-and-black, non-venomous kingsnake of Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and northern Mexico. It is resistant to pit viper venom and can eat young rattlesnakes.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 3 to 4 ft (0.9 to 1.2 m), but up to about 6.8 ft.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Central Texas to south-eastern Arizona, and north-central Mexico.

habitat.text: Any rural habitat in its range, but most often in moister places such as near water tanks and along streams.

diet.text: A powerful constrictor that eats rodents, lizards, reptile eggs it smells under the ground, and smaller snakes including young rattlesnakes.

reproduction.text: Mates from March to June and lays 5 to 12 sticky eggs in late June or July, sometimes buried up to a foot deep; they hatch after about 60 days.
